messages.subject: Apparent discrepancy in copy number data (wrong sample type?)
messages.subject_clean: Apparent discrepancy in copy number data (wrong sample type?)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

we've started using TitanCNA and we recently tackled a case where we had no actual normal samples (due to the tumor type). At least for the copy number alterations analysis, we used a reference sample produced by Agilent (it's what they use in their OneSeq kits) which was analyzed exactly like the tumor samples, and used for copy number and LOH estimation.

The input files we gave TitanCNA were:

- Read count bins (either made via readCounter or through CNVkit)
- Heterozygous SNPs made by the GATK (HaplotypeCaller) on both the sample and the universal reference

This was used with a hybrid capture kit covering the exome + the OneSeq CN backbone probes, so we set the alphaK parameters to be in an exome-like setting (2500).

What we observed is a massive discrepancy between the copy number estimated by CNVkit and the one by TitanCNA: the latter shows total amplification for every chromosome, while the former shows a mainly CN neutral landscape (see attachments, for a representative example of  chr1). This does not change if we use the CNVkit output or the one made by HMMcopy. I'm fairly sure there's some systematic error going on here (our previous tests with TitanCNA in other samples of different tumors were confirmed by independent approaches).

How can we diagnose this?

messages.subject_clean: Apparent discrepancy in copy number data (wrong sample type?)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Luca,

At the moment, TitanCNA cannot handle data points (SNPs) that are homozygous in the germline.  That is, TitanCNA expects germline heterozygous SNPs. The best way to see how this can affect the analysis is to compare the allelic ratio plots between your cases (with matched normal vs no matched normal).
I'm not entirely sure what the backbone probes are but if they contain homozygous SNPs in the cancer patient's germline, then this might be why you are seeing this problem.

Here's a previous post related to this: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/titancna/H22hyxnrgZ4/7w-GNBkile8J
The poster also included some plots which highlights the homozygous SNPs due to not having a matched normal.

Hope this is a start.

Best,
Gavin

messages.subject_clean: Apparent discrepancy in copy number data (wrong sample type?)
messages.body_plain:
Hello Gavin,

> At the moment, TitanCNA cannot handle data points (SNPs) that are homozygous in the germline.  That is, TitanCNA expects germline heterozygous SNPs. The best way to see how this can affect the analysis is to compare the allelic ratio plots between your cases (with matched normal vs no matched normal).

The "backbone" is defined, according to Agilent's product specification, as "Backbone design (high-resolution or low-resolution) for identifying genome-wide CNVs", basically an additional set of baits  (covering ~16 Mbp) specific for copy number alteration and LOH detection (not necessarily targeting genes).

As for the SNPs, they were prefiltered to only keep heterozygous SNPs (that is, the files fed to TitanCNA). The distinctive factor in the "good" runs (CN correctly called) and "bad" runs (CN erroneusly called amplified) were the binned, GC-corrected reads (correction for mappability did not make a difference), with these combinations (keeping HET SNPs from exome+backbone as valid SNPs):

1. Binned reads from backbone alone: mis-called CN (amplified)
2. Binned reads from exome data alone: correctly called CN (neutral)
3. Binned reads from backbone + exome: mis-called CN

Each of these 3 combinations was aligned separately with BWA, so there were no issues related to merging of BAM files and what not. As stated earlier, binning with HMMcopy's readCounter or with CNVkit did not have any impact on this issue.

messages.body_plain:
Luca,

1) From your original post, you mentioned that there is no matched normal for this cancer patient?  HaplotypeCaller was used to determine HET sites but from which sample?  If SNPs are het in the universal reference, that doesn't necessarily help with your patient because they are not the same hets in this patient's germline.
I'm curious to see what the allelic ratio plots look like. Perhaps genome-wide plots would be helpful too.

2) When you are analyzing binned reads from exome data + backbone, are you including these backbone intervals into targeted regions during the GC-correctiong step?

Thanks,
Gavin

messages.body_plain:
Luca,

The plots are helpful.  It does appear that the homozygous SNPs at the bottom (i.e. homozygous alt alleles) are the culprit.  While using different binned regions for coverage seems to give different results, the underlying issue is with the SNPs.  Unfortunately, TitanCNA results can only be reliable if both the binned coverage data AND the SNP data are valid. It would be a straight forward extension to make TitanCNA tumor-only but I won't be able to get to this until next year.  There are other tools that are able to handle this, as I'm sure you're looking into already.

If you are only interested in the total copy number and not the allelic copy number, then you can use the results from the intermediate step.  Or, you can also consider ichorCNA which has many customizable settings with decent documentation (https://github.com/broadinstitute/ichorCNA/wiki).

Best,
Gavin
